title: Proof of y lambda closed form wenzl bridge
html:
Proof. Proof of y lambda closed form wenzl bridge

Proof

By [Wenzl 1988] (cited in [Orellana, math/9806163, Theorem on p.17]), the unique Markov trace on the type-A Iwahori-Hecke algebra in g-convention with parameter z_{\mathrm{GL}} = Q^r (1 - Q)/(1 - Q^r) has weights \omega_\lambda(Q) = s_{\lambda, r}(Q) given by the principal-specialization Schur function. By [Chlouveraki HDR Theorem 6.20 (=Juyumaya Theorem 12, d=1 case)], the type-A Markov-trace family is 1-dimensional, parameterised by z.

The convention isomorphism g = q\sigma transports \mathrm{tr}_M on \sigma-Hecke (with the \sigma-convention z) to \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{GL}} on g-Hecke (with z_{\mathrm{GL}} = q z). Both traces have the same expansion \mathrm{tr} = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda for any choice of irreducible character basis (which is intrinsic to the algebra, hence convention-independent). By uniqueness, the weights agree:

  y_\lambda^{(\sigma)} \;=\; y_\lambda^{(g)} \;=\;
  \omega_\lambda(Q) / Z, \qquad Z := \sum_\mu d_\mu \omega_\mu(Q),

normalised so \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1. \square

Specialisation at the production convention

Under convention D, z = q^3/(q^2+1), so z_{\mathrm{GL}} = qz = Q^2/(1+Q) with Q = q^2, and the defining equation z_{\mathrm{GL}} = Q^r(1-Q)/(1-Q^r) has the exact solution r = 2. The specialisation is then s_\lambda(1, Q) — a Schur polynomial in two variables — which vanishes identically for \ell(\lambda) \geq 3 and, on the two-row stratum \lambda = (n-k,k), equals

  s_{(n-k,k)}(1, Q) \;=\; Q^k \bigl(1 + Q + \cdots + Q^{\,n-2k}\bigr)
  \;=\; q^{\,n}\,[\,n-2k+1\,]_q .

The q^n cancels against the normaliser Z, leaving y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^n and y_\lambda = 0 for \ell(\lambda) \geq 3. So the row cap is not an extra hypothesis: it is r = 2, the dimension of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) fibre, read off the bridge equation itself.

Per-partition agreement at H_3, H_4, H_5 (representative entries):

See Table 2.

The two legs are the principal-specialisation route above and the q-integer closed form; they agree identically, not to a numerical tolerance, and \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 holds exactly at each n.

Table 2 previously carried a numerical witness-versus-bridge comparison agreeing to \sim 10^{-16} — y_{(3)} = 0.41539579, y_{(2,1)} = 0.28092963, y_{(1^3)} = 0.02274495, and at n = 4 the negative entry y_{(1^4)} = -0.00084253. Both legs of that comparison were convention C, excised by the owner ruling of 2026-08-09, so the agreement certified nothing about the production trace. The independent numerical leg has not been re-run: computations/wedderburn_jones_markov.py::y_lambda_at is still convention C (and truncates to 30 significant digits against a 50-dps floor), and regenerating it is a producer change, not an edit.
